text:
The Activity:

Do a presentation about an artwork. You might need to make notes to help you remember what to say, but don't write out the whole speech or you'll just end up reading it out!

What artworks could I use?

  • A drawing you have done yourself (maybe you could make a frame and put it on the wall).
  • A picture you already have on the wall in your house.
  • A picture of a famous artwork in a book or online.
  • A real artwork in a museum or art gallery.

Does my presentation have to be true?

You could do some research so that your presentation contains some factual information, or you could invent your own “facts” (even if it is a real artwork).

What should I say?

  • When the artwork was created
  • Who created it
  • What they used to make it
  • What it represents
  • Any interesting details – things that your audience might not have noticed
  • Some information about the artwork’s history – maybe it was once stolen and then found years later, or maybe it was discovered in an attic…
  • Anything else you like!

Where should I do my presentation?

It is probably best if you have either the real artwork or a picture of it so that the person you are talking to can see what you are talking about. If you have chosen an artwork in a local gallery, it could be fun to go to the gallery and do your presentation next to the real thing!
